messages:
tenant_acme: Hey team — our March invoice shows ~2.8M embedding units billed but the dashboard reports ~940k. This is a large delta, billing looks triple what the UI says. Can someone triage?
jen: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a couple example request IDs and a sample payload (no PII) so we can trace? Also, did you enable rerank or pairwise anywhere?
tenant_acme: Sample request id: req_0a9f3c. Payload (trimmed):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model":"redwood-embed-1536",
  "inputs":["short doc 1","short doc 2","short doc 3","... up to 120 items ..."]
}
```
We also have a separate rerank call where we pass a set of candidates and the query; not the same call. No pairwise flag that I'm aware of.
samir: tagging in. Quick questions: 1) were these batched by client or server-side? 2) any client retries visible? 3) approximate timeframe for the spike?
tenant_acme: Client does batch in groups of 100, around 2026-02-28 14:20 UTC most of the heavy usage happened. We do aggressive ephemeral retries on 5xx.
jen: Thanks. I'm pulling event logs for req_0a9f3c and the surrounding window. @maria can you check billing event de-duplication for requests with multiple attempts?
maria: looking now. Initial quick find: there are 3 meter events for request_id=req_0a9f3c with attempt_id values attempt_1, attempt_2, attempt_3 — each shows embeddings.count = 100. That would explain a 3x hit. But need to confirm why retries produced full-metering instead of idempotent suppression.
kevin: infra note — client idempotency key should be honored; we dedupe on idempotency_key by default, but only for identical request bodies within the same minute. If a retry changed the payload ordering (or had different metadata like X-Client-Attempt), dedupe may have failed. Any chance the SDK re-split or reordered inputs on retry?
tenant_acme: our SDK does a simple retry with the same body. No reordering intentionally.
samir: pulling full request trace from runtime. I see three attempts with the same idempotency header x-idempotency-key: abc-123 but the second attempt was routed to a fallback runtime (older instance) that returned a 5xx after partially processing. Runtime produced meter events at two stages: pre-batch-accounting and final-success accounting. The fallback produced pre-batch accounting but failed before commit; the retry then produced final commit — looks like both pre-commit and final were recorded in billing.
jen: That suggests a double-count bug: we should only emit billing events on commit. @maria is there a rule that filters pre-commit events?
maria: billing pipeline was supposed to ignore events with phase!="committed" but I see older meter emitter (deployed last month) sent phase="precommit" and our filter logic didn't match due to a casing difference ("preCommit" vs "precommit"). So precommit events slipped through.
kevin: ouch. So casing mismatch allowed precommit metrics to be accepted. That would create near-duplicate meter rows for retries and failures.
tenant_acme: interesting — but why are some vectors showing dim=768 and others 1536 on the invoice items? We use the 1536 embed model.
samir: runtime trace: when request routed to older fallback runtime it selected older embed model redwood-embed-768 as a fast fallback for degraded instances. That runtime emitted meter rows with dim=768. When the retry hit the main runtime it used redwood-embed-1536. Both were billed.
jen: So combined issues: 1) retries + precommit event leakage; 2) fallback runtime using smaller-dim model and emitting its own meter events. Together that inflates numbers and creates mixed dims on invoice.
maria: I'll run a dedupe reconciliation query to identify all events where request_id matches and phase != committed or attempt_count>1 and mark them as potential duplicates. Query I'm running:
```
SELECT request_id, COUNT(*) as cnt, array_agg(distinct model) as models
FROM billing_meter_events
WHERE timestamp >= '2026-02-28' AND customer_id = 'acct_42'
GROUP BY request_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
```
I already see ~4k request_ids with >1 events in that window.
kevin: Ops: we should proactively block ingestion of phase values that are not lowercase, and patch the emitter to use canonical lowercase. I'll open infra PR.
jen: Customer asks: Will you be able to adjust the invoice or issue a credit?
maria: Once we have the full set of duplicated events we can do a cost reconciliation. Short term we can issue a provisional credit equal to the duplicated sum where event matches same request_id and same inputs. I'll prepare a breakdown and proposed credit.
nen: (note: not a real participant)
kevin: Putting steps: 1) infra PR to canonicalize phase and reject non-committed precommit metrics (ETA 24h). 2) billing will run reconciliation and produce credit draft (ETA 48h). 3) eng-ml to add guard so fallback runtime doesn't emit final billing events unless it fully commits (samir to coordinate).
samir: I'll add logging to detect fallback model usage when customer-specified model != runtime-chosen-model and surface those for accounting. Also adding a runtime patch to avoid emitting meter events until commit.
tenant_acme: Appreciate the plan. Can you also confirm whether the rerank calls could have contributed? We do separate rerank calls after embeddings are generated.
samir: Good point — rerank in pairwise mode would bill O(n^2) pair comparisons. I checked the customer's rerank usage: they used rerank.simple (not pairwise) in March, and rerank bills show expected counts. So rerank is not the primary cause here.
jen: Action items recap for us (and visible to the customer):
- samir: runtime patch to delay meter emission until commit + logging for fallback model (ETA 72h).
- kevin: infra shader to normalize phase values at ingest + block unknown phases (ETA 24h).
- maria: run dedupe reconciliation, compute credit, and send customer a proposed adjustment (ETA 48h).
- jen: keep customer updated and request any additional request_ids for spot checks.
maria: I've queued a job to compute dedupeable_costs; provisional credit estimated at ~$13,200 for acct_42 in that window (will confirm).
tenant_acme: Thanks — please cc billing-ops on the final credit email.
jen: cc'ing billing-ops mailing list. @maria will you post the reconciliation CSV to the ticket when ready?
maria: yes, will upload to the support ticket and mark as pending approval.
billing-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0453 — duplicate-metering-due-to-precommit-leakage. Priority: P2.
kevin: I'll monitor ingestion metrics and drop rate after patch; posting logs and PR link here when ready.
tenant_acme: Thanks everyone — we'll hold on any plan changes until the reconciliation is complete. :thumbsup:
